messages.content: Write an internal proposal asking leadership for a quarter of engineering time to pay down technical debt. Around 250 words.

**Proposal: give Q3 to paying down technical debt**

I want us to spend Q3 on maintenance instead of features.

This is an argument about numbers, not principle. A year ago the median PR went from open to merge in 2.8 days. It now takes 6.2. Most of that increase is CI. The suite runs 47 minutes and fails at random on roughly one run in five, so people rerun it, switch tasks, and come back after lunch. Separately, about 40% of Q2's engineering hours went to work nobody planned: incidents, hotfixes, and long digs into why the billing service and the account service disagree about what a "customer" is.

Three fixes, in this order. Split the monolithic test suite and quarantine the flaky tests. Finish retiring the second ORM we half-migrated to in 2024. Merge the two customer models into one service.

None of this is research. We know how to do all three. We have also deferred all three four times.

The cost is real. A quarter of eight engineers is a quarter of the roadmap, and two customer commitments currently sitting in Q3 slide to Q4.

That's the trade: one visible slip now, against a delivery rate that keeps degrading. Defer again and I send this memo next year with worse numbers and a longer list.

Please decide by the 15th so we can plan Q3 one way or the other. Happy to walk through the incident data first.

— [name], Eng Lead

The figures above are placeholders. Swap in our real CI timings, incident share, and headcount before this goes out; the argument stands or falls on them.
